pillar_reactions.evidence: Delivered in full — whole-body kettlebell sessions at 30 to 40 minutes, five-to-ten-minute daily mobility protocols, and the six-month graduation framing that 'after those six months... you won't need Trevor anymore'. The prospect agreed without questions: 'No, no. I like that. It's fine.'

The what/when/how-much frame and the intermittent-fasting eight-hour window were delivered. The prospect mapped it onto his existing practice rather than questioning it — 'I do a 7-17 right now' — and accepted the sustainability point about a weekly pizza and birthday-party ice cream without pushback.

The prospect did not catch the word and the rep had to repeat it — 'Now, third part is the accountability part.' / 'The what?' / 'The accountability, yeah.' The pillar was then delivered at length (app, form-check videos, weekly check-ins, Trevor's personal cell number) and the prospect's only response was off-topic — 'I watch all the videos' — after which the rep moved straight to 'that's it, there's nothing less, nothing more for me to cover'. The single pillar that most directly answers his real gap, that nobody is coaching the guy who writes everyone else's programming, did not land.

anchors.raw: we moved our office in november we build a complete gym so you know i go there every morning 6 a.m
anchors.note: He owns the gym he trains in and already trains daily at no marginal cost, so $6,000 buys programming and coaching only — not access, not equipment, not the habit. The rep never repriced the offer against that, which left the number sitting against a zero-cost baseline.

anchors.raw: there's a lot of people that i know that come to the gym that depend on me i'm putting the program together right
anchors.note: He is the person others rely on to write programming. That makes him self-sufficient on the deliverable being sold and is the strongest latent objection on the call — it was never surfaced or reframed.

anchors.raw: I've looked at a lot of programs. I just want to make sure this is what I want to do.
anchors.note: An active comparison set the rep never got a name or a number for. He asked what the prospect was comparing on and stopped at the first answer, so the corpus records that competitors exist in this deal without recording who or at what price.

anchors.raw: I did a long, probably eight years, nine years ago, I used to go to this gym where there was a lot of kettlebell workouts.
anchors.note: He has done kettlebell work before and liked it, which removes the unfamiliar-modality risk that blocks other prospects in this corpus. He pre-sold himself on the method — 'I just saw the videos and I thought it was, I just like that'.

unmet_demand.want: To be training and set up before departing on a month-long boat trip on July 9th, nine days after the call
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Nothing structural blocks it — the rep committed to a Trevor onboarding call within roughly 24 hours of payment and the app travels on a phone. The gap is that the prospect asked 'how do we get all this set up in less than a week?' and did not visibly register the answer as settled; he was still citing 'this vacation thing' as a reason to think two minutes later.

unmet_demand.want: Variety and novelty in training — 'it just gets boring after a while, I like doing different things'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: This was the first thing he said when asked what brought him in, and it is the one thing he named twice. The pillar presentation answered time-efficiency, sustainability and accountability but never answered boredom. Steel maces were mentioned once in passing as something he would learn; the programme almost certainly does serve this, and nobody said so.
